richOriginalExamples: Original IM 2021 G5 U05:L13 Analyze Addition Mistakes: analyze why RIGHT-aligning a decimal with fewer printed decimal digits than the other addend breaks place-value meaning. Decimal POINTS must be aligned, adding trailing zeros when useful; a result being larger than one input alone does not validate it.

Warm-up Estimation Exploration Many Places original 1,987.89+658.54=2,646.43. A reasoned benchmark e.g2000+650≈2650 sets scale; pupils mark too-low/about-right/too-high estimates and justify before exact arithmetic. This original task replaces invented42.8+6.15 comparisons, which remain optional examples.

Activity 1 Compare Calculations original 621.45+72.3=693.75. Elena incorrectly right-aligns last printed digits and obtains628.68; her claim it is plausible because greater than621 is mathematically insufficient. Andre correctly aligns decimal PLACE VALUES and gets693.75, consistent with approx620+70≈690. Teacher asks who is correct and the exact column and rounding evidence.

Activity 2 Same Digits Different Sums original four addition expressions: 2.63+7.74=10.37,26.3+774=800.3,46.3+31.42=77.72,463+3.14=466.14. The same digits have different magnitude depending on decimal point placement; students should explain whole and fractional places in each and estimate reasonableness.
